## Body

**Security: block** at `703cde7710d62080907527de0e426e3d2fbe5c26` (plan 224, migration 0046).

Rendered nudge bodies contain holding/claim labels, idle duration and fixed daemon instructions, not cards, notes or request bodies. However, an unrelated local-origin sender can suppress the new prime FYI without impersonating its holder or the daemon.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| 1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | crates/daemon/src/idle_nudge.rs; crates/store/src/queue.rs | 263; 1220-1243 | Predictable daemon FYI ID is externally reservable; collision silently drops the prime notice but reports Held | 9/10 |

## S189-001: notification-ID preemption

The new prime FYI uses `idle-nudge-fyi:<holder>:<anchor>:<prime>`. Holder/prime identities and the last own-event sequence are public metadata. An admitted daemon-key caller can send an ordinary FYI **as itself**, to another valid recipient, with this future ID.

External send admission refuses `from=pij-bg`, but does not reserve this ID prefix. Local-origin messages must use `from_machine: None` (`crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1937-2000,2386-2415`).

The FYI store keys by `(origin, id)`, not sender or recipient (`crates/store/migrations/0027_fyi_origin.sql:18`). Both the ordinary local FYI and the daemon FYI use the empty local origin. `INSERT OR IGNORE` therefore inserts nothing for the legitimate notice after the earlier reservation. `Delivery::hold_fyi` still returns `Held` without verifying that the existing row belongs to this sender/recipient (`crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:817-831`).

The legitimate prime has no pending copy: the preexisting row targets the other recipient. The already-committed `(seat, anchor)` mark prevents another attempt, and the nudge audit records a held prime FYI. The holder's normal nudge can still arrive; the bypass suppresses its prime's oversight notification.

No victim identity assertion, victim-message read, token theft or process control is required. Paired origins cannot occupy the empty local-origin key this way. This is a new notification-admission/integrity failure, not C32's accepted identity-only residual.

Protect daemon notification identity from external reservation, or use an unguessable occurrence identifier unavailable before admission. Deduplication must not accept an existing different sender/recipient as successful admission of the daemon notice. Test an ordinary preseeded FYI to another recipient, then assert the real prime receives the intended daemon notice and that audit status reflects actual admission.

## Labels and disclosure

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Seat/prime and holding labels | Holder seat uses `SeatId::rendered`; role, instance, project and claim-kind components use the closed word renderer. Malformed stored components become `invalid (N chars)`. Claim-number formatting emits digits only. |
| Extra private prose | Neither body includes card `did`/`next`, state notes, claim subjects, queued request bodies, files, context sizes or delivery error text. |
| Recipient control | Stored project prime IDs select live recipients; the live parent is fallback only when no project's prime is selected. No new caller-supplied recipient argument exists. |
| Cross-project labels | Every selected project prime receives the **complete** holder label list, not a per-project subset (`idle_nudge.rs:179-190,213-223,262`). This remains within the packet's labels/idle-time content scope; project-isolated disclosure is not implemented or certified. I do not assume a project-confidentiality rule absent from the stated contract. |
| Wider legacy FYI pipeline | Direct body labels are protected, but the existing large-batch FYI recovery command still interpolates a raw legacy recipient ID (`crates/core/src/fyi.rs:123-126`). No separate new exploit is established here. |

No changed-line C19/C21 disclosure was established. The full-label fanout is recorded as a scope qualification, not a separately proven unauthorized secret read.

## Caller control, audit and reliability

There is no new external mark/reset endpoint. Legitimate own reports/activity and owned jobs can suppress or re-arm the holder's own stretch. Existing public-identifier replay paths retain their prior registration-strength/F88 limitations; they are not being reintroduced as new findings. Their recorded report/activity events and existing grant-audit behavior remain.

Reader ACK, FYI and delivery events are not own activity. The query excludes idle `seat.activity`, so passive idle heartbeats do not restart the quiet stretch.

The conditional mark is parameterized and cancellation-owned, persisted before sends. This prevents duplicate attempts after restart/overlap, but refusal or cancellation after marking can spend the attempt; prime rotation does not resend that stretch's notice. Those are reliability limits, distinct from S189-001's adversarial reservation.
